item.title: Global cities seek new partnerships in China's Ningbo
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
NINGBO, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- As driverless trucks carried containers along preset routes and gantry cranes worked overhead at Ningbo-Zhoushan Port's Meishan terminal, Romulus Agbedjekou was thinking of a harbor thousands of kilometers away in Benin. "This is one of the most modern ports in the world," said Agbedjekou, special representative of the mayor of Cotonou and chair of the city's economic affairs commission. Impressed by the automated equipment at the East China Sea port in Zhejiang Province, he said he hopes to replicate some of the practices at his country's Autonomous Port of Cotonou. His interest reflects a practical focus of the 2026 Global Mayors Dialogue, which brought mayors and representatives from 20 cities in 15 countries to Ningbo in Zhejiang from Nov. 2 to 5. They came with different priorities, from making ports more efficient to helping smaller companies use new technology. Fourteen cooperation projects were signed during the gathering, covering trade, technology, education, tourism and exchanges between local governments. Ahmed Wazeery, secretary-general of Suez Governorate, Egypt, talked about his nation's Suez Canal Economic Zone, with six ports and four industrial areas, and the China-Egypt TEDA Suez Economic and Trade Cooperation Zone, where investment has exceeded 6.7 billion U.S. dollars. Wazeery saw opportunities to expand cooperation with Ningbo beyond industry and manufacturing, particularly in education, cultural industries and high-tech industrial parks. In a different setting on Wednesday, an embodied AI robot holding a pen drew a crowd at a smart factory operated by PIA Automation. The machine wrote steadily on paper as visiting officials leaned in to watch or raised their phones to record it. Enrico Ricci, representing the mayor of Florence, Italy, was impressed by the robot's movements and ability to interact. Florence, he said, is also looking for ways to connect advanced digital technologies with small businesses and startups, and hopes to exchange more ideas with Ningbo. Ningbo already has extensive international business links. Mayor Shen Mingquan said the eastern Chinese city trades with more than 220 countries and regions. More than 5,000 Ningbo-based enterprises have invested overseas, while nearly 10,000 foreign-invested firms operate in the city. New Zealand's Auckland Mayor Wayne Brown stressed the importance of personal connections in trade. "Trade today is becoming more city to city, and it's people to people connections which contribute to this trade," he said. He recalled exchanges between Ningbo and the city of Waitakere, now part of Auckland, that predated their 1998 sister-city agreement. Waitakere's then-mayor, Bob Harvey, had made several visits to Ningbo, helping promote exchanges in education and sports. Brown said Auckland is also exploring ways to use technological innovation to drive business growth and hopes to learn from its Chinese partners. Among the new arrangements announced in Ningbo were friendly exchange ties between the city's Yinzhou District and Saint-Étienne-du-Rouvray in France, and between Yuyao City (under the administration of Ningbo) and Errachidia in Morocco. Delegates also issued the Ningbo Consensus on Collaborative Development, calling for open trade, industrial cooperation and closer people-to-people exchanges. For Joachim Moyse, mayor of Saint-Étienne-du-Rouvray, such cooperation ultimately comes down to the relationships cities build with one another. He described his task as building bridges between people. ■

item.description:

item.title: China passes law to prevent, punish cross-border corruption
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-06
BEIJING, Nov. 6 (Xinhua) -- China's top legislature on Friday adopted a law to combat cross-border corruption. The law aims to prevent and punish cross-border corruption, deepen international anti-corruption cooperation, safeguard China's sovereignty, security and development interests, and promote the building of a fair and equitable global anti-corruption governance system. With 47 articles in six chapters, the law covers mechanisms and responsibilities, case handling and international cooperation, integrity and compliance, legal liability, among other areas. The law was passed at a legislative session of the Standing Committee of the National People's Congress. ■

item.title: Hainan's new offshore duty-free policy logs 5 bln USD sales in first year
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-05
HAIKOU, Nov. 5 (Xinhua) -- Duty-free shopping by local residents of south China's Hainan Province has evolved from occasional purchases into regular daily consumption, data released by Haikou Customs show. From November 2025 to October 2026, offshore duty-free shopping in Hainan hit 33.45 billion yuan (about 4.98 billion U.S. dollars), with 4.88 million shoppers purchasing 27.64 million items, a year-on-year growth of 13.8 percent, 8.6 percent and 2.4 percent respectively. China adjusted its offshore duty-free shopping policy for travelers departing Hainan, effective from Nov. 1, 2025, expanding the duty-free goods categories to 47. Six types of domestic products, including silk scarves, ceramics and tea, are also eligible for sale via offshore duty-free channels. Sales of newly added categories under the policy reached 210 million yuan, while domestic goods sold through duty-free channels registered 240 million yuan over the period. The revised policy allows Hainan residents with an offshore travel record within a calendar year to purchase unlimited "buy-and-take" duty-free goods in the same year. Haikou Customs recorded 410 million yuan in "buy-and-take" purchases by the island residents in the period. A total of 24,000 outbound travelers made duty-free purchases worth 160 million yuan in the 12 months, facilitated by Hainan's visa-free entry arrangements and expanding international air routes. Under Hainan's visa-free entry policy, eligible travelers from 61 countries may enter Hainan through its open ports without a visa and stay within the province for a maximum of 30 days. The Hainan Free Trade Port officially launched island-wide special customs operations in December last year. According to plans, China aims to build Hainan into a globally influential tourism and consumption destination by 2035. ■

item.title: Xi Focus: Unlocking a vast market for the world
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-04
SHANGHAI, Nov. 4 (Xinhua) -- After a journey of more than two months across continents and oceans, machinery from WFL Millturn Technologies cleared customs in Shanghai last month for this year's China International Import Expo (CIIE), carrying the Austrian manufacturer's hopes of expanding further into Chinese and wider Asia-Pacific markets. "I don't see any good reason why we will not be successful in China in the upcoming decades," said WFL Managing Director Stefan Hackl. His company will make a double debut: its first appearance at the import expo after more than 20 years in the Chinese market, and the Asian debut of its brand-new machine tool. The company's confidence is rooted in part in the vision behind the CIIE, an initiative championed by Chinese President Xi Jinping, who has personally planned and steered its development. Designed to give overseas businesses greater access to the vast and growing Chinese market, the expo has increasingly turned China's development into opportunities for the world. Now in its ninth year, the CIIE has become a regular fixture on the global trade calendar. Running from Nov. 5 to 10, the expo will bring together 4,142 overseas exhibitors, including more than 2,000 first-time participants like WFL. In the weeks leading up to the expo, shipments from around the world continued to arrive in Shanghai, bringing in a diverse range of products, from Peruvian bananas and French tires to Australian coffee and Kazakh ice cream, all ready to meet buyers at the event. As the world's first national-level exhibition dedicated to imports, the CIIE offers a compelling response to rising protectionism and trade barriers. Rather than viewing trade as a competition for a limited share of global demand, it seeks to make the world economic pie bigger by creating opportunities for businesses and economies to grow together. "Our aim is to turn the China market into a market for the world, a market shared by all, and a market accessible to all," Xi has said. "This way, we will be able to bring more positive energy to the global community." A PROMISE KEPT In his keynote speech at the opening ceremony of the first CIIE in 2018, Xi said the expo is "an important decision made by China to pursue a new round of high-level opening-up, and is China's major initiative to still widen market access to the rest of the world." "China's initiative to expand imports is not a choice of expediency. It is a future-oriented step taken to embrace the world and promote common development," Xi said, pledging that the event would be held annually and "feature good performance, good results and continued success in the years to come." Eight years on, the CIIE has grown into a premier global platform for trade, investment and cultural exchanges, connecting businesses, innovators and consumers from around the world. The promise of an annual expo with lasting results has been borne out by its growth. Past editions have drawn more than 180 countries, regions and international organizations and seen more than 3,400 new products, technologies and services make their debut, while cumulative intended deals have exceeded 580 billion U.S. dollars, according to the organizer. "The CIIE is far more than a trade show," said Jérôme Vanachter, president of Lesaffre Greater China. The French yeast maker is back for a ninth consecutive edition this year. Calling the expo a "market-intelligence hub," Vanachter said the CIIE helps turn market insights into products. Past expos have also seen Xi announce a series of opening-up measures, including advancing the development of pilot free trade zones and the Hainan Free Trade Port (FTP), continuously trimming the negative lists for foreign investment, and expanding the opening of telecommunications, healthcare and other services. These pledges were followed by concrete actions. In November 2024, China removed the last two manufacturing-related restrictions from its national negative list for foreign investment. Last December, the Hainan FTP launched island-wide special customs operations, a milestone in China's drive for high-standard opening-up. "Today, the CIIE has become a showcase of China's new development paradigm, a platform for high-standard opening-up, and a public good for the whole world," Xi said at the fifth edition of the event in 2022. The role of the CIIE in China's opening-up agenda is expected to continue in the years ahead. In its five-year development blueprint for the 2026-2030 period, the country has called for expanding imports and continuing to hold the CIIE and other major trade fairs, including the Canton Fair in south China, while strengthening trade-promotion platforms. A MARKET SHARED BY ALL "Economic globalization represents the trend of history," Xi said at the second CIIE in 2019, likening it to the world's great rivers -- the Yangtze, the Nile, the Amazon and the Danube, which all "surge forward in relentless flow, and nothing can stop their mighty movement." China has been translating this vision into action by opening wider. Quality products from an increasing number of countries are finding a foothold in the Chinese market, generating profits for businesses, wages for workers and tax revenues in their home countries. For 17 consecutive years, China has remained the world's second-largest importer. Also in the first three quarters of 2026, the country's imports rose 22.3 percent year on year, significantly outpacing export growth. "The vastly huge China market is the most promising in the world," Xi noted at the third CIIE in 2020, citing the country's huge population and vast middle-income group. The country's retail sales of consumer goods surpassed 50 trillion yuan (about 7.44 trillion U.S. dollars) for the first time last year, and are expected to grow by another 10 trillion yuan over the next five years. The appeal of the Chinese market is reflected in the growing participation of global businesses in the CIIE, which has attracted a record number of more than 300 Fortune Global 500 companies and industry leaders this year. In terms of exhibition space, U.S. exhibitors lead for the eighth consecutive year, occupying more than 50,000 square meters, while companies from Germany, the United Kingdom and France also rank among the top participants. Over 480 products are set to make their global, Asian or China debut at the event, the highest number in history, underscoring the Chinese market's growing role as a launchpad for global innovation. Under Xi's leadership, China has also sought to make the opportunities offered by its market more accessible to developing countries. For years, the CIIE has provided free exhibition booths to exhibitors from the world's least developed countries. This year, according to the organizer, the exhibition area for African businesses is set to increase steadily, while the space allocated for free booths for the least developed countries will expand by 17 percent. An official delegation from Cote d'Ivoire will make its first appearance at the CIIE's business exhibition this year, showcasing cocoa, coffee, cashews and kola nuts. In May, a zero-tariff policy took effect on imports from all 53 African countries with which China has diplomatic relations. "We are very happy to participate for the first time," said Rami Koné, an official with the country's export agency. "This will be a good opportunity to showcase Cote d'Ivoire to the world." "Of the problems confronting the world economy, none can be resolved by a single country alone," Xi once said. "We must all put the common good of humanity first rather than place one's own interest above the common interest of all." As Xi has pledged, China will continue to open its arms to the world, offering countries greater opportunities for market access, investment and growth. "Together, we can achieve development for all," he has said. ■

item.title: Xi holds talks with Sultan of Oman, stressing bilateral cooperation, peace efforts in Middle East
item.description:
Published: 2026-11-02
Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026. (Xinhua/Li Xiang) BEIJING, Nov. 2 (Xinhua) -- President Xi Jinping said on Monday that China stands ready to work with Oman to steer their strategic partnership to a higher level, and to help restore peace and realize lasting stability in the Middle East at an early date. Xi made the remarks during talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China -- the first by Oman's head of state since the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries 48 years ago. The talks constituted an important chapter in the history of China-Oman relations and will inject strong impetus into the development of bilateral ties, Xi said. He said China and Oman should enhance political mutual trust and strengthen exchanges of experience in national governance, while expressing China's support for Oman in safeguarding national independence, sovereignty, security and stability, and in independently exploring a development path suited to its national conditions. The two sides should expand practical cooperation and continuously cement the foundation of mutually beneficial and win-win cooperation, he said, adding that China is committed to promoting high-quality development and expanding high-standard opening up, which will bring greater opportunities to Oman and other countries. China is ready to deepen the synergy of development strategies with Oman and be a stable and reliable partner in the energy sector, a partner with promising potential in investment, and a partner in fostering innovation within advanced technologies, he said. China aims to make bilateral energy cooperation more multi-dimensional and comprehensive, strengthen exchanges in industry, investment, artificial intelligence (AI), science and technology, and people-to-people ties, and join hands on the paths toward development, revitalization, and modernization, Xi said. He also called for efforts to intensify cooperation in such fields as education, tourism, health, media and sports, to continuously substantiate the China-Oman strategic partnership. Xi noted that the Middle East and the Gulf region should not become an arena for major power rivalry or geopolitical conflicts, and that concerted efforts are needed to foster and maintain peace and stability in the region. "China has been actively committed to ending hostilities and promoting peace, aiming to contribute its wisdom and solutions to resolving the regional security predicament," Xi said. China will continue to advocate resolving disputes through political and diplomatic means, and support regional countries in building a common home of good-neighborliness, development, security and cooperation, he added. China is ready to strengthen communication and coordination with Oman and other Arab states and Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) countries to jointly work for the early restoration of peace and tranquility in the region and the realization of lasting stability, Xi said. Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said that Oman firmly adheres to the one-China principle and supports China in safeguarding its national sovereignty and territorial integrity. He expressed hope that this visit will serve as a new starting point to explore more cooperation opportunities with China, and build a future-oriented partnership and promote greater development of bilateral relations. Stressing that China has been Oman's largest trading partner for many years and Chinese enterprises' investment in Oman has kept growing, Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik said Oman is ready to synergize development strategies with China and strengthen cooperation in trade, investment, industry, infrastructure, AI, science and technology, and other fields. He said Oman highly appreciates China's just position on the Middle East issue and stands ready to maintain close coordination with China to uphold international law, advocate for the peaceful resolution of disputes, and jointly promote security and stability in the region and beyond. After their talks, the two leaders jointly witnessed the signing of cooperation documents covering areas including industrial and supply chains, green development and digital finance. During the visit, the two sides issued a joint statement on deepening the China-Oman strategic partnership. Prior to the talks, Xi held a welcome ceremony for Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik in the Great Hall of the People. Xi also held a welcome banquet for him at noon. ■ Chinese President Xi Jinping holds talks with Sultan Haitham Bin Tarik Al Said of Oman, who is on a state visit to China, at the Great Hall of the People in Beijing, capital of China, Nov. 2, 2026.
